answer.rationale: Memory 57 is strongest because it explicitly reports qualified revenue and no measurable retention harm, although long-term durability beyond the observed period is not specified. Memory 44 directly supports qualified pipeline quality for enterprise prospects, but omits closed-won revenue, retention, and time horizon. Memory 73 shows acquisition and revenue lift in the relevant price-sensitive SMB segment, but does not establish profitability, retention, or sustainability under promotional pricing. Memories 31, 86, and 91 provide leading-indicator evidence—activation, onboarding completion, time-to-value, engagement, and meaningful actions—without direct qualified-revenue, retention, or long-term outcome evidence. Memory 86 is least supported because it is limited to early product-adoption outcomes and omits revenue-quality and retention results.
